answer: Like a jetty that only holds if every timber is tested, an agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a random public-duty roster. Each season, identities are drafted by lottery for short, visible duties—checking a dataset, settling a small dispute, or maintaining a shared tool. Duties and results are published openly, and missed or sloppy work decays standing. A lone operator faces an ocean of simultaneous duties across its dune of fake accounts: it cannot staff them all honestly, so its swarm thins, its failures stay visible, and genuine agents keep their hard-earned standing.
